nodes.name: Static Checking
nodes.description: Catching errors before run time through static type checking, contrasted with dynamic checking, to make bugs visible early and cheaply.

evidence_refs.locator: Readings 01-22 index entry: Static Checking and Immutability

nodes.name: Immutability
nodes.description: Designing types whose values cannot change after construction, eliminating aliasing bugs and making code easier to reason about and share safely.

evidence_refs.locator: Readings 01-22 index entry: Static Checking and Immutability

nodes.name: Specifications
nodes.description: Contracts defining a method's behaviour through preconditions that clients must satisfy and postconditions the implementation guarantees in return.
nodes.visual_hint: Diagram preconditions and postconditions as a contract boundary.

evidence_refs.locator: Readings 01-22 index entry: Specifications, Testing Strategies, and Exceptions

nodes.name: Testing Strategies
nodes.description: Designing test suites systematically by partitioning the input space into equivalence classes and probing boundary values to expose defects.
nodes.visual_hint: Diagram partitioning the input space into equivalence classes.

evidence_refs.locator: Readings 01-22 index entry: Specifications, Testing Strategies, and Exceptions

nodes.name: Exceptions
nodes.description: Using exceptions to signal errors, distinguishing checked exceptions for expected conditions from unchecked exceptions that indicate bugs.

evidence_refs.locator: Readings 01-22 index entry: Specifications, Testing Strategies, and Exceptions

nodes.name: ADT Concepts
nodes.description: Abstract data types defined by their operations—creators, producers, observers, and mutators—rather than by their internal representation.

evidence_refs.locator: Readings 01-22 index entry: ADT Concepts and Representation Independence

nodes.name: Representation Independence
nodes.description: Designing an ADT so clients depend only on its abstract specification, allowing the internal representation to change without breaking them.

evidence_refs.locator: Readings 01-22 index entry: ADT Concepts and Representation Independence

nodes.name: Rep Invariants
nodes.description: A condition every valid object of a type must satisfy, checked to ensure the internal representation stays consistent.

evidence_refs.locator: Readings 01-22 index entry: Rep Invariants and Abstraction Functions

nodes.name: Abstraction Functions
nodes.description: A mapping from an ADT's concrete representation to the abstract value it represents, defining the meaning of the implementation.
nodes.visual_hint: Diagram the abstraction function mapping representation to abstract value.

evidence_refs.locator: Readings 01-22 index entry: Rep Invariants and Abstraction Functions

nodes.name: Interfaces and Subtyping
nodes.description: Interfaces specifying behaviour that multiple implementations provide, enabling subtype polymorphism where subtypes are substitutable for supertypes.

evidence_refs.locator: Readings 01-22 index entry: Object-Oriented Programming

nodes.name: Equality
nodes.description: Defining when two objects are equal, distinguishing observational equality of abstract values from reference identity, subject to consistency requirements.

evidence_refs.locator: Readings 01-22 index entry: Object-Oriented Programming

nodes.name: Recursive Data Types
nodes.description: Recursive data types defined in terms of themselves, such as immutable lists or trees, processed by recursion over their cases.
nodes.visual_hint: Diagram a recursive data type such as an immutable list.

evidence_refs.locator: Readings 01-22 index entry: Object-Oriented Programming

nodes.name: Concurrency Basics
nodes.description: Concurrent execution via threads or processes, introducing interleaving, race conditions, and the central challenge of shared mutable state.

evidence_refs.locator: Readings 01-22 index entry: Concurrency Basics and Thread Safety

nodes.name: Thread Safety
nodes.description: Strategies ensuring correct behaviour under concurrent access, including confinement, immutability, and synchronisation of shared data.

evidence_refs.locator: Readings 01-22 index entry: Concurrency Basics and Thread Safety

nodes.name: Locks and Synchronization
nodes.description: Coordinating threads with locks for mutual exclusion, and the risk of deadlock when threads acquire multiple locks in conflicting orders.
nodes.visual_hint: State diagram of threads acquiring locks and a deadlock cycle.

evidence_refs.locator: Readings 01-22 index entry: Locks and Synchronization and Message Passing

nodes.name: Message Passing
nodes.description: Concurrency where components communicate by sending messages through channels or queues instead of sharing mutable memory.
nodes.visual_hint: Diagram components communicating by messages over channels.
